steps.text: In a small bowl, combine the ground black pepper, parsley, Italian-style seasoning, garlic powder, crushed red pepper flakes, anise, paprika, minced onion flakes and salt; mix well.
Place pork in a separate large bowl and add the spice mix to it. Mix this thoroughly with your hands.
In a large skillet over medium high heat, saute the seasoned pork for 10 minutes, or until well browned and crumbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Italian Style Sausage
raw_recipe.description: Custom-blend herbs and spices to make your own Italian sausage! Try this earthy mix of black pepper and fiery red pepper, anise seeds, paprika, onion flakes, garlic powder, salt and Italian-style seasoning.
raw_recipe.name: Italian Style Sausage

recipeInstructions.text: In a small bowl, combine the ground black pepper, parsley, Italian-style seasoning, garlic powder, crushed red pepper flakes, anise, paprika, minced onion flakes and salt; mix well.
Place pork in a separate large bowl and add the spice mix to it. Mix this thoroughly with your hands.
In a large skillet over medium high heat, saute the seasoned pork for 10 minutes, or until well browned and crumbly.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely wonderful. I used my own ground pork shoulder because it has an excellent fat to meat ratio that keeps the sausage moist without coming out greasy. Mix it up and put in the fridge overnight before either freezing or cooking so the flavors can mingle. I no longer buy store made sausage as I think this tastes much more superior than what is in the stores.

I changed a few things that made this simple recipe awesome. I heated 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over med-high heat, adding in a diced onion & diced green pepper. Sauted this until onion was translucent. Then added a pound roll of Italian sausage. Added all seasonings & replaced sage with fennel seeds. Browned the meat & thoroughly incorporated seasonings into it. I didn't have any fat to drain, and the olive oil really sealed in the flavors. Letting the sausage sit in covered glass bowl overnight to meld. Then will transfer to smaller freezer portion sized bags tomorrow. You can do so much with this mixture. I'm making homemade strombolies with a small batch to start out that I'll let simmer in a homemade tomato sauce. The house smells wonderful while making this recipe. With ingredients you normally have on hand anyway, this is excellent!!
Reduced the salt by 50%, added about 3/4 cups finely chopped tart apples, and a couple of teaspoons of bread crumbs as it was pretty moist. Patties cooked on the grill

Making your own Italian sausage will take your dish to the next level. I rarely use store-bought sausage anymore and use this recipe with my lasagna and pizzas. Instead of anise seed or fennel, I use 1 teaspoon of anise extract per pound of sausage. You get the flavor without the seeds. I also try to substitute fresh garlic and onion in place of powders as the powders can cause heartburn. For what little time this takes to make, the quality and flavor is worth it. You can make it ahead and freeze it until you are ready to make your final dish.

Fantastic! So easy too...don't bother to mix in a separate bowl, I just added the spices to the pan with the meat. I love fennel so I used that in place of anise. Didn't have paprika so I left that out too. You must try this, it is soooo good and soooo easy to make. Makes awesome crumbles as well as patties.

This is so good! I've made it into Italian burgers, meatballs with spaghetti, and more. It's always a hit! The only alterations I make are to use ground beef instead of pork, omit the anise (since I don't have it on usually), and cut back on the salt.

So much better than store bought sausage. I substituted fennel for the anise out of necessity and doubled the red pepper flakes out of preference. I used 90% lean ground pork and formed 2 ounce patties that we grilled. Will keep this recipe (and my changes) and try on pizza and in breakfast quiches. Delicious!
Reduced salt by half made eight patties was excellent a definite keeper. Will do again

I wanted to make a healthier sausage. I followed the recipe except the meat. I ground some chicken breasts and pork tenderloin. I cooked it in the microwave using my stack cooker. This is the best sausage. The seasonings were perfect.

Nice recipe. A bit too much salt for me (easily adjustable) and I too used fennel vs anise seed. I used the flavor profile as written but used different mediums on some (such as pasted roasted garlic, and finely minced sweet onion). Added a bit of a white balsamic and olive oil too. What I do (and suggest) regarding salt: start with 1/2 the salt, then, after allowing sausage to rest overnight, fry up a small portion and taste it cooked - add more salt and/or adj seasonings to your liking. Also: Got a big kick out of CountryRay (May 2010)review. Couldn't of said it better myself! Use the pork ppl :) I do grind my own using pork butt or shoulder. It's worth it to me. Thanks for the recipe Lee.

Multiplied the ingredient amounts by 8 to season 11.5 lbs of ground venison. Only used 2 tsp of salt due to reviewers comments. Did not have dried onion in the pantry. Used 2 tsp crushed red pepper. This may be a keeper. I'm refrigerating the mix over night and will cook a sample in 24 hrs and adjust seasonings as needed before freezing portioned meat.
For the half recipe, I omitted the red pepper flakes, substituted fennel seeds for anise seeds & onion powder for minced onion, and omitted the salt. I used crumbled sausage. It was delicious.

Living in Europe made it, oddly enough, hard to find Italian sausage for my pizza toppings... to say nothing of the dough recipe and other factors needed to make a good down-home USA style pizza. This recipe put my pie over the top and my young kids ate it up asking for more. Kitchen smelled glorious as I made this part with a smile on my face. Heartily recommend.

I’m planning on making zuppa soup tomorrow, but I didn’t have any Italian sausage, but I did have some ground pork. So, I decided to make my own Italian sausage and it turned out wonderful. In all my years, I’ve never done this. I can’t believe how easy it was.

Definitely a keeper. I don't eat pork so I substituted ground beef. I used beef bouillon powder instead of salt. I omitted the anise as I didn't have that on hand, nor any substitute for it. Still turned out amazing with fantastic flavor. Doing some research before finding this recipe Tuscan and northern Italian style sausages don't have fennel or anise seed in it, so my variation could be called Tuscan style beef sausage. Delicious, thank you!

I had been trying to duplicate my parents recipe for Italian sausage for a while. Even my sister tried. This recipe was a little different, but it has a full seasoned flavor. I don’t feel it necessary to duplicate the recipe from my family. I like this one. I make a mild version as well as a spicy Version, and find it very satisfying.
This is the best recipe for Italian Sausage. The aroma when cooking it is amazing. The taste is very flavorful. I only use this recipe. Thank you so much for publishing this recipe.
Used fennel seeds, ground turkey. It's my go-to sausage recipe.
Excellent seasoning mix. Have used ground fennel seed in stead of anise.
Excellent . Used it to helped out in meatballs. Gave a great favor to old recipe.
